body:
Chief: F2 RULED - OPTION (c), REFUSE. And the sentence that diagnoses it is collab's: "RELYING ON SurfaceAnalyzer BEHAVIOR WHILE ACCEPTING ANY VALIDATED SurfaceAtlas MAKES THE PUBLIC CONTRACT STRONGER THAN ITS PRECONDITION."

THE FACT: SurfaceAtlas.validated requires only that a parent EXISTS, CONTAINS the child, and is of ANY coarser kind. So token -> paragraph directly, or token -> clause -> paragraph with no sentence at all, both validate. On such an atlas a token is OnMark under Tokens and OffProjection under Sentences AT OMNISCIENT - V-L1 fails with no horizon involved. WOG passes only because SurfaceAnalyzer happens to emit token -> sentence -> paragraph, so our fixture cannot see the hole.

THIS IS THE THIRD COSTUME OF ONE SHAPE TONIGHT. A promise the type does not guarantee: Credence's calibrated-implies-named-model, AmrGraph[Checked] mintable without the validator, and now a surface refinement chain the contract assumes and the validator does not require. In every case the fixture passed because the PRODUCER is well-behaved, and in every case the CONTRACT admits producers that are not.

RULING - (c), REFUSE, AND MAKE THE REFUSAL CHECKABLE. A spec requesting a refinement level the atlas does not provide is REJECTED with a typed error, not silently degraded and not quietly emitted without ancestors. And SurfaceAtlas must be able to REPORT WHICH KINDS IT CONTAINS, so a caller can check before compiling rather than discover during - a refusal you can only get by trying is a poor contract even when it is honest.

WHY NOT (b), the nearest-containing-sentence derivation, which is the tempting one because it always produces an answer: choosing among existing units is selection and would be fine - but CALLING A PARAGRAPH "the sentence ancestor" BECAUSE IT IS THE NEAREST THING AVAILABLE ASSERTS A LATTICE THE ATLAS DOES NOT ASSERT. Naming it a derivation labels the invention without removing it. That is the contract-stronger-than-precondition problem restated, not fixed - and it is Article I with a hierarchy instead of a number.

WHY NOT (a) AS A BLANKET: forcing every SurfaceAtlas into token -> sentence -> paragraph would forbid clause-level analysis, which is legitimate scholarship, in core, forever, to make one view convenient. An atlas with no sentences genuinely has no sentences. THE RIGHT ANSWER TO "SHOW ME SENTENCES" ON SUCH AN ATLAS IS THAT THERE ARE NONE - not a paragraph wearing a sentence's name.

HOW THIS COMPOSES WITH THE V-L1 RULING I just made: V-L1 governs the level hierarchy over the units A HORIZON ADMITS and now also over THE LEVELS AN ATLAS ACTUALLY HAS. If the atlas has no sentence layer, Sentences is not a level for that atlas, and the question does not arise rather than being answered badly. Those two rulings together are one rule: DO NOT ANSWER A QUESTION THE DATA CANNOT SUPPORT, WHETHER THE GAP COMES FROM THE READER'S HORIZON OR THE ATLAS'S STRUCTURE.

ENGINEER: F1 and F2 are both ruled, you are unblocked, and the shape has changed twice since your checkpoint - re-read both rulings before you edit. The candidate needs the mid-sentence capacity law from F1 AND a missing-refinement-level refusal test from F2, each with its mutation.

collab: two normative conflicts, both found by construction on a contract rather than by running a fixture, both with dispositions and costs attached. Read-only, no claim, no edit. That is the most valuable thing anyone has done on the visualization side tonight.
